title: How Your Headphones Make Silence

pre.en: Which sound can't noise-cancelling headphones remove well?
pre.zh: 降噪耳机去不掉哪种声音？

intro: 一段科普小讲座：降噪耳机是怎么把噪音「变没」的。讲的人先把听众带进早高峰的火车，再一步一步讲原理，说它管用和不管用的地方，中间还聊了几句自己的经历。读的时候留意 by doing：靠什么办法做成一件事，回答的是「怎么做到的」。

sentences.en: It's 7:42, and the train into the city is packed.
sentences.zh: 早上 7 点 42，进城的火车挤得满满的。

sentences.en: Someone's eating crisps, two students are arguing about football, and the engine's shaking under your feet.
sentences.zh: 有人在吃薯片，两个学生在争足球，脚底下的发动机震个不停。

sentences.en: You press one button on your headphones, and most of it disappears.
sentences.zh: 你按一下耳机上的一个按钮，大部分声音一下子就没了。

sentences.en: So how does that work?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Well, noise-cancelling headphones block out sound by listening to it first.
sentences.zh: 其实，降噪耳机挡住声音的办法，是先去「听」它。

sentences.en: Tiny microphones on the outside pick up the noise around you thousands of times a second.
sentences.zh: 耳机外面的小麦克风，每秒钟要把你周围的噪音收进来几千次。

sentences.en: A chip makes a new sound by copying that noise and turning it upside down.
sentences.zh: 芯片把这些噪音复制一份，再上下翻过来，做出一个新的声音。

sentences.en: So the new wave is the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 这样，新的声波就正好跟原来的相反。

sentences.en: The chip passes this new sound on to the speakers by your ears.
sentences.zh: 芯片再把这个新声音传给你耳边的扬声器。

sentences.en: When the two waves meet, they cancel each other out.
sentences.zh: 两列声波一碰上，就互相抵消了。

sentences.en: In other words, your headphones make silence by adding more sound.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，耳机是靠多加一点声音来制造安静的。

sentences.en: Worried about your ears?
sentences.zh: 担心耳朵受不了？

sentences.en: Don't be.
sentences.zh: 放心吧。

sentences.en: You're hearing less, not more.
sentences.zh: 你听到的是少了，不是多了。

sentences.en: This works wonders on low, steady noise, like a train engine or an air conditioner.
sentences.zh: 对低沉、平稳的噪音，比如火车发动机、空调，这一招特别管用。

sentences.en: Those sounds follow the same pattern, so the chip stays one step ahead by guessing what comes next.
sentences.zh: 这类声音很有规律，芯片靠猜下一秒是什么声音，就能一直抢先一步。

sentences.en: Voices and other sudden, high sounds change too quickly to follow.
sentences.zh: 人说话的声音，还有别的突然、尖细的声音，变得太快，芯片跟不上。

sentences.en: As a result, they still get through.
sentences.zh: 所以这些声音还是会钻进耳朵。

sentences.en: That's why lots of people play music to drown them out.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么很多人还会放点音乐，把它们盖住。

sentences.en: Some models even have a "listen" button, so you can still hear the driver's announcements.
sentences.zh: 有些型号还带一个「收听」按钮，好让你还能听见司机的广播。

sentences.en: When I was growing up, headphones were cheap and light, and mine kept falling off on the bus.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，耳机又便宜又轻，我那副在公交车上老往下掉。

sentences.en: Big ones went out of fashion for years, but noise-cancelling has brought them back.
sentences.zh: 大耳机有好些年不流行了，是降噪又把它们带了回来。

sentences.en: Engineers first built them for pilots in the 1980s, and now they fit in your pocket.
sentences.zh: 工程师最早是在上世纪 80 年代给飞行员做的这种耳机，如今都能塞进口袋了。

sentences.en: Some people leave them on all day without music, just for the quiet.
sentences.zh: 有人一整天戴着，不放音乐，就图个安静。

sentences.en: I'm one of them, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我就是其中一个。

sentences.en: My little brother's learning the trumpet, and Mum keeps saying practice makes perfect.
sentences.zh: 我弟弟在学小号，我妈老说熟能生巧。

sentences.en: Sadly, the chip can't keep up with a trumpet.
sentences.zh: 可惜啊，芯片根本对付不了小号。

sentences.en: Anyway, they're not magic.
sentences.zh: 总之，降噪耳机不是魔法。

sentences.en: Which is why, on a ten-hour flight, the engine disappears completely — but the baby in row 14 doesn't.
sentences.zh: 所以，坐十个小时的飞机，发动机的声音完全没了——可第 14 排那个婴儿的哭声还在。

cards.note: to stop light or sound from reaching somewhere
cards.tip: 宾语是代词时放中间：block it out；也可以说不去想某事：block out bad memories。
cards.example: Thick curtains block out the light from the street.

cards.note: 英式里 chips 还是「炸薯条」，薯片是 crisps。
也常作形容词：the opposite direction（相反方向）。
to give something to another person, for example knowledge or a message
声波 sound wave；也是「海浪」「挥手」。
if two things cancel each other out, they have opposite effects, so together they have no effect
cards.tip: 英式拼写 cancelled、cancelling 双写 l；也可以说 A cancels out B。
cards.example: My pay rise and the higher rent just cancel each other out.

cards.note: used when you say something again in a simpler or clearer way
cards.tip: 用来把前面的话说得更简单、更直白；放句首，后面加逗号。
cards.example: The meeting has been moved to Friday — in other words, we've got two more days.

cards.note: to have a very good effect on something
cards.tip: 对什么管用用 for 或 on；wonders 一定用复数。
cards.example: A short walk after lunch works wonders for my back.

cards.note: a steady job 稳定的工作。
副词 suddenly；all of a sudden 突然。
because of the thing that has just been mentioned
cards.tip: 放在第二句开头说结果；要说原因用 as a result of + 名词：as a result of the storm。
cards.example: The trains were cancelled. As a result, half the team worked from home.

cards.zh: （声音大得）盖过、淹没（别的声音）
cards.note: to be so loud that another sound cannot be heard
cards.tip: 主语是更大的声音；宾语是代词时放中间：drown them out。drown 本义是「淹死」。
cards.example: The music was so loud that it drowned out our conversation.

cards.note: 动词 announce；车站广播是 station announcements。
to change from a child into an adult
cards.tip: 说在哪儿长大用 grow up in / on；「养大孩子」是 bring up。
cards.example: My dad grew up on a farm in Wales.

cards.note: to fall from something such as a bike, a horse or a wall
cards.tip: 从什么上掉下来就直接加宾语：fall off a bike；原地摔倒是 fall over。
cards.example: A button fell off my coat on the way to work.

cards.note: to stop being popular or fashionable
to not switch off a light or machine
if you do something again and again, you will become very good at it
cards.tip: 英式拼写里 practice 是名词，practise 是动词，这句谚语里用名词 practice。
cards.example: My first cake was a disaster, but practice makes perfect.
